insight: First-pick Keeper works best with Storm Spirit and Ember Spirit in mid lane. Amplify magic damage with Solar Bind while stacking and using Chakra Magic to enable spell spam from your laner.
Build Holy Locket early to maximize healing value from Illuminate spam, then play fast with map control through double stacking.

matchup_context: against physical damage carries like Ursa and Clinkz
insight: Use Disruption to waste enemy BKB time and dispel Fury Swipes from Ursa. Disseminate amplifies damage to targets while spreading damage to allies, synergizing with tanky offlaners.
Shadow Demon lacks lockdown for highly mobile heroes, making it reliant on teammates to provide catch. Use Disruption reactively to save teammates instead.

Flex Tusk between position four and five. Tag Team or Drinking Buddies provides burst damage in lane, while Snowball saves multiple teammates (better than single-target disruption) but vulnerable to AoE silences.
Avalanche is now a ground-target stun affected by status resistance, not mini stuns. This effectively doubles crowd control time without requiring Toss combo, making position four Tiny viable.

Play Treant like Bounty Hunter with invis repositioning. Punch applies Leech Seed as a bind/disarm (unique utility), and Living Armor provides 420 damage block at level 5. Use Aghanim's Shard for map vision and bait value.

Bat Rider sees more play because Shadow Demon is heavily banned. Napalm in lane enables blink dagger into early roaming and initiations. Best against mobile mid heroes that Shadow Demon would normally counter.
Instant hex into blink lasso drag is one of the best catches for mobile mid heroes. Benefits from Shadow Demon bans since Disruption previously countered your shackle.
Learn to auto-attack harass without drawing creep aggro instead of overly relying on spells. This enables early kills with fast level 6 into slow, silence, and ultimate combo.

Consider Kaya build to spam Q for farming speed instead of maxing slow/silence. Add Meteor Hammer to solo push objectives when team is passive. Maintain flexibility to build utility (Blink Dagger) when needed.
Chain stun with Bushwack follow-ups for easy initiation. Combine Acorn Shot right-click damage with gush-provided negative armor for surprising burst damage in lane.
Better than Hoodwink versus mobile mids since Deadshot is harder to dodge if they don't see it coming. Close range silence forces them into fights where you can silence and chain damage them.
Ultimate immunity to physical damage provides superior survivability compared to other high-damage supports, especially against top physical damage carries.
Track gold enables fast tempo building compared to Treant. Similar playstyle but weaker laning stage. Cannot be early-picked like Treant due to locked position four.
Laning stage is least punished in pubs. Farm to Dagger at your own pace, then solo delete enemies with invis assassinations. Creep drag through weak lane to reach impactful mid-game.
Use Serpent Wards to solo push objectives when team is jungling. Drop wards and push independently until you take structures.
Maledict Cask combo enables lane kills. Ultimate requires enemies to avoid standing next to each other and position around it, which low-bracket pubs fail to do, enabling high win rates.
Awkward laner but provides BKB-piercing bashes and guaranteed charge/ultimate for roaming. Fairly global with ability to split push lanes and still charge to join fights.
Enemies don't understand Phoenix's mechanics, leading to free kills and high win rates. Benefits from buffed Radiance and Holy Locket itemization for healing support playstyle.
Surprisingly high win rate in pubs despite complexity. Don't need to use Relocate frequently; just provide massive healing with meta items. Low-bracket enemies don't target heal enough.
Power Cogs value is misunderstood by pub enemies. Provides insane utility from single hero through Cogs, Hook, and Swap mechanics. Punishes bad positioning.
High execution requirement to play as proper support without scaling greedily. Can punish positioning with teleportation but easily becomes greedy. Prefer other heroes for more reliable play.
Support Invoker's value is limited to Cold Snap and Earn early game. After this, flexibility increases with Shard and Force Staff builds. Purple Facet Mind of Eirauqs enables better scaling.
Strong hero but requires both execution (balancing Song) and team coordination. Enemies don't understand Largo but teammates must, limiting pub win rate. Works best when team commits to objectives.

Most pub players play position four like position five (defensive, no roaming). Actual position four heroes require creep dragging, roaming, and fast-paced teamplay, resulting in lower win rates in pubs.

Flexible supports like Wind Ranger and Dark Willow can scale, but going full damage every game is greedy grief. Recognize when to build utility (Blink, Force Staff) versus scaling based on game state.

At Archon and lower, play position five heroes with high win rates instead of struggling with position four execution. Learning proper position four playstyle (creep dragging, roaming) requires deliberate improvement.
